summary: Go from an empty VS Code window to a CMSIS solution that builds and debugs
triggers: start a new CMSIS project for a board
get_session_status says that no folder is open
unmapped: Keil Studio Pack (`Arm.keil-studio-pack`): CMSIS Solution extension, CMSIS Debugger, Arm Tools Environment Manager
vcpkg-configuration.json naming CMSIS-Toolbox, CMake, Ninja and GCC from the Arm tools registry
verification: a CMSIS solution that is open in a VS Code window, builds with `cmsis_action build`, and reaches `main` with `cmsis_action load_and_debug`.
`cmsis_action { action: 'build' }`. The first build resolves packs and can take minutes: a result with status `running` is not a failure, `cmsis_action { action: 'status' }` waits for it.
stop_conditions: When a procedure is not in the index, say so and do not improvise its steps.
Ask the user to install the **Keil Studio Pack** (`Arm.keil-studio-pack`) from the Extensions view and to reload the window.
**An existing project.** Ask for its folder or its `*.csolution.yml`, then go to step 6.

**A new project.** Ask for the board, or the device when there is no board: the name printed on it, the manufacturer, and the revision when known; the parent folder and a project name (letters, digits, dash, underscore); the compiler, when the user has a preference: `GCC`, `AC6`, `CLANG` or `IAR`; how it will be debugged: the probe on the board or on the desk (CMSIS-DAP, ST-Link, J-Link, ULINKplus, …), or an Arm FVP simulation model.

`FAIL` because a tool the manifest names is not installed yet: open the folder with `cmsis_action {action:'open_solution', path:'<folder>'}`, and ask the user to answer the prompts of the Arm Tools Environment Manager in the new window (download, licence).
Any other `FAIL`: report it and stop.

When the board has no BSP example and its DFP has no startup component, `$start-cmsis-project` reports that the minimal project cannot be created. Tell the user, and offer `$add-board-layer` after a solution exists, or a template of the pack.

When `cmsis_action build` still answers `[CMSIS_NO_SOLUTION]` with "A solution file exists", wait ten seconds and try again, at most three times; then read `get_recent_problems` and report what the extension said.
Neither procedure in the index (`knowledge_get` fails for both): ask the user to choose the debug adapter in the CMSIS view under **Manage Solution Settings**.
Ask the user to connect the board.
When the session does not start, read the hint of the result and `get_recent_problems`; for a probe or connection failure continue with `$debugger-troubleshooting`.

extracted.title: No folder open or no solution loaded: NO_WORKSPACE and CMSIS_NO_SOLUTION
extracted.body:
| Sign | State |
|---|---|
| `Workspace: no folder is open`, or `[NO_WORKSPACE]` from a tool | No project is open in the window |
| `[CMSIS_NO_SOLUTION]` with "contains no *.csolution.yml" | A folder without a solution |
| `[CMSIS_NO_SOLUTION]` with "A solution file exists" | The solution is not loaded |

A window needs some seconds after it opens. Call `get_session_status`. When `cmsis_action build` still answers `[CMSIS_NO_SOLUTION]` with "A solution file exists", wait ten seconds and try again, at most three times; then read `get_recent_problems` and report what the extension said.

extracted.title: Compiler line in a CMSIS vcpkg-configuration.json
extracted.body:
For another compiler replace the GCC line:

| Compiler | Line in `requires` |
|---|---|
| `AC6` | `"arm:compilers/arm/armclang": "^6.24.0"` |
| `CLANG` | `"arm:compilers/arm/llvm-embedded": "^17.0.1"` |
| `IAR` | none: remove the line, the user provides the compiler |

The file only names the tools. The Arm Tools Environment Manager fetches them when the folder is opened in VS Code.

extracted.title: Which window cmsis_action open_solution uses
extracted.body: A folder that a window already has open is used there, and the solution is made the active one. Any other folder opens in a new window. The window you started in stays as it is; this session's later calls go to the new window. `list_debug_windows` shows both.
